newsitem.title: UK: Siemens UK wants Britain in EMU - report.
newsitem.headline: Siemens UK wants Britain in EMU - report.

text.p: The plans of Siemens UK to invest up to one billion stg in Britain and create 4,000 new jobs will be at risk if the UK government does not take part in European monetary union, the Observer reported on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted Siemens UK chief executive Jurgen Gehrels as saying that as a major exporter the company needed exchange rate stability.
"If Britain decides not to join the single currency it will definitely affect our investment decisions in the future," said Gehrels.
"I am quite sure the same applies to others -- especially companies that serve not just the UK market but world markets."
The Observer said the German electrical engineering group currently employed 14,000 people in Britain.
